Si j’ai décidé de revenir sur la mort de: I decided to revisit the death of Nooran Rezayi because it raises important questions that go beyond the events of September 21 alone. Behind the investigation by the Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes (BEI), which has just concluded, and the one by the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM), which is still ongoing, there is also a community trying to understand what happened and what this tragedy reveals about its relationship with institutions.
Pour écrire cet article, j’ai tout d’abo: To write this article, I first put together a timeline of events and went through the information made public by the BEI, as well as the statements of the Minister of Public Security. I also gathered reactions from the Rezayi family through their lawyers, spoke with a former police officer who is now a criminology lecturer to better understand how investigations and the use of force work, and met with residents on the ground in Longueuil to take the pulse of the community.
Plusieurs des personnes approchées, nota: Several of the people I approached, including young people who knew Nooran and residents of the neighbourhood, chose not to speak publicly. Their silence is also part of what this story tells. As is often the case at La Converse, my intention is to document the facts while making room for the questions that remain open in society.
<strong>Près de six mois après la mort d: Nearly six months after the death of teenager Nooran Rezayi, the investigation has just reached a new stage. On March 11, 2026, the Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes (BEI) announced that it had sent its report to the Director of Criminal and Penal Prosecutions (DPCP), who is responsible for deciding whether criminal charges should be laid.
<strong>Mais au-delà de cette étape judi: But beyond this judicial step, the account of the events remains partly fragmented: a tight timeline for the intervention, a parallel investigation, recent search warrants and lingering questions in the community, which is still trying to understand what happened that day.
Le<l1> communiqué du BEI</l1> marque la: The<l1> BEI news release</l1> marks the end of the investigation into the police intervention and the start of a waiting period for the family, which hopes to get answers. “The family has taken note of the end of the BEI investigation and the transmission of its report to the DPCP, except for two expert reports that will be sent later. For the family, many questions remain, both about the sequence of events and the reason given to justify the fatal shot, as well as about the investigations that followed,” said the legal team representing the Rezayi family. At this stage, the details that would explain what the officer says he perceived as an imminent threat at the moment of the shooting are not public.
Le drame du 21 septembre commence par un: The tragedy of September 21 begins with a 911 call reporting a group of young people in a residential neighbourhood in the Saint-Hubert borough of Longueuil. The caller describes 15 to 20 young people wearing surgical masks and armed with baseball bats and cayenne pepper. The call, which lasts about 10 minutes according to the<l1> written transcript from the 911 call centre obtained by Radio-Canada</l1>, also alleges the presence of a firearm. That claim was refuted two days later by BEI director Brigitte Bishop, who said the only firearm found at the scene was that of the officer who shot the child.
Lorsque des auto-patrouilles du Service: When patrol cars from the Service de police de l’agglomération de Longueuil (SPAL) arrive on the scene, an officer opens fire. Nooran Rezayi, 15, is fatally struck by two bullets. A video of the scene, filmed by a surveillance camera, was made public at a news conference held on December 9 by the Rezayi family and their lawyers, M<sup>e</sup> Virginie Dufresne-Lemire and M<sup>e</sup> Fernando Belton. It shows that barely 10 seconds go by between the arrival of the police and the two fatal shots.
Voilà pourquoi la famille Rezayi accuse: That is why the Rezayi family accuses SPAL officers of using unreasonable and disproportionate force by opening fire so quickly, and twice, on Nooran. In the wake of this, the family announced it is filing a civil suit against the City of Longueuil and the officers involved in the intervention. It is seeking $2.2 million in damages.
Comme le prévoit la loi au Québec lorsqu: As provided by law in Quebec when a police intervention results in a death, the case was immediately handed to the BEI. The agency is responsible for determining whether the officer’s use of force was justified in the circumstances.
Dans les jours qui suivent, l’affaire su: In the days that followed, the case stirred strong emotion in the community.<l1> Gatherings and public speeches were held to demand answers</l1>. Doubts about the system’s ability to deliver justice began to be voiced, all the more so because similar cases, notably that of young<l2> Fredy Villanueva</l2>, have had controversial outcomes. Just three days after Nooran’s death,<l3> an online petition was launched demanding an independent investigation</l3> by an impartial law firm, the determination of responsibility and sanctions against those responsible.
Les soupçons s’accentuent quand Catherin: Suspicions grew when Catherine Fournier, the mayor of Longueuil, learned in November that 90 minutes had passed between the gunshots and the call made by SPAL officers to notify the BEI of the incident. Citing “<l1>alleged breaches of the SPAL’s legal and regulatory obligations,” the mayor turned to the Minister of Public Security</l1>, Ian Lafrenière, asking that an investigation be opened into her city’s police force.
À l’époque, le ministre avait dit vouloi: At the time, the minister said he wanted to wait for the BEI report to be filed. This week, Mr. Lafrenière said in a statement sent by his office that “everything is ready to [...] launch [the investigation].” However, he specified that it would take place only once the usual checks are completed in order to “make sure the file [is] complete for the DPCP.”
Pour comprendre ce qui se joue dans ce d: To understand what is at stake in this case, one must distinguish between two different investigations. The first is the BEI’s, which examines the legality of the officer’s use of force. The second seeks to reconstruct the events that preceded the intervention: Who was there? Why were the police called? What happened before they arrived? It is the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) that the BEI tasked with conducting this parallel investigation.
Pour André Boisjoly, ancien lieutenant-d: For André Boisjoly, a former SPVM lieutenant-detective who is now a lecturer at the École de criminologie of the Université de Montréal, the two parts complement each other.
« L’enquête du BEI se concentre sur un m: “The BEI investigation focuses on one precise moment: the one when the officer decides to shoot. The question is whether, with the information he had at that moment, the use of force was justified,” he explains.
Les policiers parlent alors de « continu: Police officers then speak of the “use-of-force continuum,” a gradation of the means that can be used when facing a threat. “Drawing your weapon is one thing, firing is another. You have to look at whether other intermediate means could have been used,” he adds.
Le 26 février dernier, plus de cinq mois: On February 26, more than five months after the events, several searches were carried out on Montréal’s South Shore by the SPVM, which is responsible for investigating the circumstances that preceded the police intervention. This step has revived attention around the case. The reasons behind the searches and their results remain secret. The SPVM said that “since the investigation is still ongoing, no assessment of the searches can be provided at this time.”
Mais selon André Boisjoly, « le mot clé,: But according to André Boisjoly, “the key word is ‘corroboration.’” In his view, investigators aim to gather items that can confirm or disprove certain information obtained earlier. And those can be various kinds of items: clothing, objects or even electronic devices. “If someone says, for example, that a text message was sent or that a call was made, police may want to recover the phones to verify that information,” he says.
Avant de procéder à une perquisition, le: Before carrying out a search, however, police must obtain a warrant authorized by a judge. “You have to convince the judge that the step is relevant and show that the items being sought could be admissible as evidence. It’s not a fishing expedition,” the former police officer insists.
Les perquisitions ont été menées plus de: The searches were carried out more than five months after the events. According to André Boisjoly, however, that is not unusual in a criminal investigation. “It’s never too late to carry out a search. But the sooner it’s done, the better,” he says. In some cases, evidence can be found several years after the events. “As long as the evidence hasn’t been altered, it can remain relevant,” he says.
Cependant, ces délais peuvent aussi deve: However, such delays can also become a legal issue. Indeed, Mr. Boisjoly concludes, “a defence lawyer could challenge the relevance of evidence collected late.”
De son côté, Alexandre Popovic, porte-pa: For his part, Alexandre Popovic, spokesperson for the Coalition contre la répression et les abus policiers (CRAP), believes these searches are a diversionary tactic. “To make people forget this tragedy,” he says, “they’re trying to manipulate public opinion and make people believe that the real danger doesn’t come from a police officer using deadly force against an unarmed teenager, but that the danger comes from Nooran’s friends.”
<strong>La décision maintenant entre les: The decision is now in the hands of the DPCP
Avec la transmission du rapport du BEI,: With the BEI report sent over, the case now enters a phase of analysis by the Director of Criminal and Penal Prosecutions (DPCP).
Le rôle du procureur consiste à examiner: The prosecutor’s role is to examine the investigation’s findings and determine whether the evidence gathered justifies laying criminal charges.
« Le rapport établit essentiellement s’i: “The report essentially establishes whether or not there are elements of negligence and makes recommendations. But the final decision belongs to the prosecutor,” André Boisjoly explains.
Le DPCP peut également demander un compl: The DPCP can also request further investigation if it considers that certain information needs to be clarified before it makes a decision. Indeed, the SPVM’s investigation into the events that preceded the police intervention is still ongoing.
Le rapport du BEI ne sera toutefois pas: The BEI report will not, however, be made public. The agency says it contains sensitive information, including statements from witnesses and police officers as well as evidence gathered during the investigation. This means the detailed findings of the investigation will remain confidential, a situation that fuels some questions in the community.
Interrogé par <em>La Converse</em>, le B: Asked by La Converse, the Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes (BEI) explains that its investigation reports cannot be made public in their current form. The agency specifies that these documents contain statements from witnesses and people involved, as well as physical evidence and expert reports that could be used in possible criminal proceedings.
Selon le BEI, caviarder ces rapports ne: According to the BEI, redacting these reports would not make their release any more feasible. “A large majority of the information would be removed,” the institution says, which would run counter to the goal of transparency. The agency says, however, that it is open to a change in the law that would eventually allow it to publish an adapted version of its reports.
Les données publiées sur le site du BEI: The data published on the BEI’s website also shows that the information made public varies depending on the nature of the interventions. In cases involving injuries, some details about the investigation are sometimes released. By contrast, when a police intervention involving a firearm leads to the death of a civilian, BEI news releases repeat almost word for word the same explanation. The agency says the report sent to the Director of Criminal and Penal Prosecutions contains “the statements of the witnesses and police officers involved, the physical evidence gathered and the related expert reports.” Since these items are deemed sensitive and protected by confidentiality rules, the BEI says that “no additional information drawn from the investigation will be disclosed.”
Pour certains observateurs, cette situat: For some observers, this situation fuels a sense of uncertainty. “It’s total fog. The institution refuses to give out information,” says Alexandre Popovic.
Au-delà des procédures judiciaires, près: Beyond the judicial proceedings, nearly six months after the events, several elements of the story remain hard to piece together publicly. In the community’s eyes, many questions remain unanswered. Indeed, behind the procedures and the expert reports, there are still voices that have barely been heard. Nooran’s young friends, whom we tried to speak to, have retreated into silence since the tragedy. Some people close to him describe a climate of fear and caution as the investigation continues. On the ground, several residents whom La Converse tried to approach also declined interview requests, citing their weariness with a case that continues to mark the neighbourhood.
La blessure demeure ouverte pour toute u: The wound remains open for an entire community. At a time when public reports point to a rise in violence among young people in Longueuil, some residents also say they sense a weakening of trust between part of the city’s youth and law enforcement.
Au-delà de l’enquête judiciaire, ces sil: Beyond the judicial investigation, these silences and worries sketch the portrait of a local community still searching for answers, and perhaps also for a dialogue that remains to be rebuilt.
Depuis la création du Bureau des enquête: Since the creation of the Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes (BEI) in June 2016, 68 people have died during police interventions in Quebec. In 54 of these fatal situations, police officers fired their guns. In these cases involving fatal police shootings, 18 reports have been sent to the Director of Criminal and Penal Prosecutions (DPCP). Forty-two files have been closed without any criminal charges being laid, while eight decisions are still pending and two investigations are ongoing.
